subject: Temporary headroom surge bridge request for latency-sensitive sprint
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary headroom surge bridge request for latency-sensitive sprint

Hi team,

NebulaHealth is kicking off a 72-hour low-latency sweep next Tuesday (2026-12-01) to validate a new checkout flow that will be extremely sensitive to tail latency. They asked for a short-term Dedicated capacity window to avoid cold-start jitter during the live validation.

Ask: can we provision a temporary dedicated headroom slice (equivalent of 8 A100-class GPUs / ~32 vram-equivalents) from 2026-12-01 00:00 UTC for 72 hours (drop at 2026-12-04 00:00 UTC)? They are willing to accept an autoscale-exception for that window and sign an MOU for the added cost.

What I need from you:
- Jonas: feasibility + runbook for a transient carve (how we would isolate + preemption policy)
- Kimberly: product-side approval for autoscale-exemption and guidance on any routing/fallback we should enforce
- Marcus/Soojin: a quick estimate of unit cost and whether this conflicts materially with other Q4 pilots (we need to know if we must move any queued pilots)

Attachments: q4_headroom_matrices.xlsx (workload shapes), slo-impact-diagram.png

Why this matters: NebulaHealth is a strategic pilot for our enterprise play in health; the validation impacts a potential Dedicated contract. If we can keep tail P95 latency under 120ms during this test we increase the likelihood of a 12-month reserved contract.

I know this is a short notice ask — if we can get a plan by EOD Monday (2026-11-30) I will coordinate the customer comms.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary headroom surge bridge request for latency-sensitive sprint

Laura — thanks for the heads up. A few clarifying Qs before we lock anything down:

1) Workload shape: the attached matrix shows hourly token QPS and tail latency targets. Can you confirm expected sustained QPS and spike profile (e.g., 90th percentile of requests that will hit the Dedicated pool)?
2) Fallback behavior: is the customer OK with an automatic fallback to a lower-capacity model variant if we see DSAT risk?
3) Billing: do we want to charge as Dedicated short-term reservation (pass through to Nebula) or absorb as a pilot credit?

Operationally, I want to avoid changing global autoscale policies unless necessary. Two mitigations to consider that reduce the request size: pre-warming with warm-up traffic, and temporary KV-prefix caching for repeated prefixes. If those cover 60–70% of the burst, we may be able to do a smaller carve (4 GPUs vs 8).

Jonas — can you estimate runbook complexity for both options (8-unit carve vs 4-unit + caching)? If the ops overhead for the larger carve is high, we should prefer mitigations.

If we can get the numbers by EOD Monday I'll make a call on the billing approach and loop in Finance.

—Kimberly
Director, Product (Dedicated)
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, gcp-sales@cloudvendor.com, ops@nimbushealth.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary headroom surge bridge request for latency-sensitive sprint

Laura / Kim — quick ops read: feasible, with two options and trade-offs.

Option A (fast, higher cost): carve a transient Dedicated slice of 8 A100-equivalent units from our staging buffer.
- Isolation: dedicate a transient subnet+pool and pin NebulaHealth model instances.
- Autoscale policy: set a local override (no cross-tenant autoscale) for the 72-hour window. Fallback: if overall cluster pressure > 70% we preempt this slice gracefully (notify customer 10 min prior).
- Impact: will temporarily reduce available burst headroom for other pilots; estimated probability of needing to move one small pilot = 20%.
- Ops runbook effort: ~3 engineer-hours to provision + 1 on-call for the window.

Option B (lower cost, lower ops): allocate 4 A100-equivalent units + KV prefix warm cache + conservative batching tweaks.
- Isolation: smaller transient slice + caching layer deployed on same pool.
- Autoscale: minimal override needed; rely on cache to reduce token throughput.
- Impact: small chance tail latency still spikes without more caching work.
- Ops runbook effort: ~5 engineer-hours up front for cache instrumentation + 1 engineer on-call.

Estimated cost (back-of-envelope for 72h):
- Option A: $18k (pass-through to customer)
- Option B: $9k (pass-through to customer) + ~8 engineer-hours of engineering time

We should contact gcp-sales@cloudvendor.com to confirm physical host availability for the week of 12/1. I can open the purchase/commit ticket and tag INF-4921.

Next steps proposed:
1) Kimberly: pick Option A (safer) or B (more cost-efficient) by EOD Monday.
2) If Option A: Marcus to confirm which queued pilot to reprioritize (if any).
3) I'll prepare the runbook and a short MOU template; Laura to sign customer-facing approval.

Jonas
Senior Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary headroom surge bridge request for latency-sensitive sprint

Thanks Jonas — that framing is helpful.

Decision: go with Option A (8-unit carve). NebulaHealth prioritizes reliability for this validation and will cover the pass-through as a short reservation.

Action items I’m assigning:
- Jonas: please open INF-4921 and attach the runbook + MOU draft. Proceed with provisioning as soon as GCP availability is confirmed.
- Marcus/Soojin: confirm which queued pilot we'll nudge and send me the final cost passthrough figure (I need it before the customer call Monday).
- Kimberly: once runbook is attached to INF-4921, please sign off on the autoscale override and we will issue the MOU to NebulaHealth.

I’ll take point on customer comms and the MOU signature. Marcus — please copy Finance on the cost breakdown.

Laura
Sr. Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
